title: SummitCare renewal & geocluster capacity review
next_steps: Jordan to send draft extension SOW and pricing by 2026-02-12
Priya to share benchmark spreadsheet and APAC latency runbook by 2026-02-13
SummitCare to confirm go/no-go for APAC region by 2026-02-20
action_items: Jordan: Prepare SOW that includes 20% capacity uplift and APAC geocluster option - due 2026-02-12
Priya: Run targeted latency/cost benchmarks for their 512-token workload in ap-northeast-1 and share results - due 2026-02-13
Mark: Share network egress constraints and procurement timing for KMS/HSM integration - due 2026-02-17
transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-02-10 16:00 UTC
- Duration: 42 minutes
- Attendees: Jordan Park (Redwood AE), Priya Nambiar (Redwood SE), Evan Li (Redwood CSM), Alice Moreno (SummitCare Head of ML), Mark DeWitt (Infra Lead), Sonal Iyer (Procurement)

Auto-generated summary (optional):
SummitCare is approaching renewal; they want a 20% committed capacity uplift, evaluate APAC region activation (ap-northeast-1) and discuss contract extension terms. Security (SOC2, KMS), latency SLOs, and cost tradeoffs were discussed. Action items captured.

Topics:
- Renewal timing & contract amendment
- Capacity uplift sizing and burst policy
- APAC geocluster activation and data residency
- Security/KMS and audit logs
- Benchmark plan and next steps

[00:00] Jordan: hey everybody, thanks for joining. quick agenda, we'll run through the renewal ask, APAC onramp, and then Priya will talk perf/benchmarks. sound good?
[00:18] Alice (SummitCare): yep thanks Jordan, we wanted to make sure we had time to walk through the uplift and the timeline cause procurement needs dates.
[00:32] Priya: cool. quick note that we've got the Redwood dedicated — sorry Redwood Ded pool — options and also the private VPC flow. i'll show latency numbers from last month but we need to run a short apac test.
[00:50] Mark (SummitCare): one clarifying Q, when you say apac region activation, is that full private VPC or just hosted endpoints in ap-northeast-1?
[01:05] Jordan: good Q. we can do either. recommended pattern for you is dedicated geocluster (we call it geocluster) with VPC peering for data controls. if you want full private - on-prem style - we can discuss private plane install but that's more involved.
[01:23] Sonal: procurement will need contract dates. our renewal window is end of feb, we need a signed amendment by 2026-02-26 ideally.
[01:35] Jordan: understood. that's tight but doable. we can draft an amendment for the 20% uplift and APAC add-on and send by friday.
[01:48] Priya: on perf, the last benchmark we ran on your 512-token prompt mix showed median p95 latency at 110ms in us-west-2 on our quantized path, with cost per 1k tokens at $0.55 equivalent. moving to ap-northeast-1 we expect p95 to be ~130-150ms for same instance types. but there's an extra egress and network overhead to plan for.
[02:10] Alice: 130-150ms p95 is ok, most of our interactive flows tolerate it. our main concern is the batch reranking path where latency spikes matter.
[02:26] Priya: for reranking we recommend splitting workloads: serve short queries in apac region, and large rerank batches on dedicated us-west pools with cross-region KV cache prefetch. that reduces tail on critical paths.
[02:44] Mark: cross-region KV cash? did you say KV cash — i think you mean KV cache — our infra doc had questions on cache coherency.
[02:56] Priya: yep KV cache, bad transcribe there. for coherency, we suggest async invalidation and a short TTL for keys that are frequently updated; it's what our runtime uses in geocluster mode.
[03:12] Jordan: folks, i want to call out SLOs. You currently have a 99.5% latency SLO in the contract; adding APAC geocluster requires us to set region-level SLOs and an explicit fallback policy (route to us-west-2 on error). is that acceptable?
[03:29] Alice: yes, fallback to us-west is acceptable for now as long as we get clear RTOs and an SLA on failover. also audit logs retention must be 1 year to meet our compliance.
[03:41] Evan (CSM): we can include 12-month audit log retention in the amendment as an add-on. i'll flag the pricing.
[03:50] Sonal: on pricing - we're evaluating Infralayer and BigCloud AI; Infralayer's pitch is cheaper per-token but they don't have the same KV cache optimizations. we want a map of tradeoffs.
[04:07] Jordan: totally. we'll share a side-by-side: latency vs unit cost, and note hidden egress/peering fees. Priya has the benchmark sheet.
[04:18] Priya: i also want to call out quantization choices — your model variants run best on 4-bit q8-like profiles for cost, but for highest quality we keep an fp16 fallback. mixing them gives best $/quality.
[04:34] Mark: do you support customer's KMS or must we use Redwood KMS? we need HSM-backed keys for token encryption.
[04:44] Jordan: you can bring your own KMS; we have integrations for AWS KMS and external HSM via KMIP. for private deployments we support customer-managed HSMs. please send specifics.
[04:56] Mark: we'll share the KMS architecture diagram after this call.
[05:03] Alice: on throughput, we need to guarantee sustained 1.2k rps for short prompts during peak. is that within the proposed 20% uplift?
[05:14] Priya: so the 20% uplift as a committed token capacity is a first pass. for burst and autoscale we can add burst capacity of 2x for brief windows; if you need sustained 1.2k rps we might need a 35% uplift or a dedicated slot reservation across more GPUs.
[05:32] Jordan: summary — base amendment will propose 20% committed cap + optional burst commit to be negotiated. Priya will attach perf numbers showing gap.
[05:42] Sonal: procurement question: will expanding to APAC change our billing currency or invoicing?
[05:50] Jordan: not necessarily; we can keep USD billing but can add region-specific billing lines for your internal chargeback. if you need local currency invoicing we can route through our APAC billing partner, but that adds lead time.
[06:05] Alice: also need SOC2 attestation updated. do you have a fresh report?
[06:12] Evan: yes we do, current SOC2 Type II report is available; i'll drop the link. we'll also share our ISO snippets if helpful.
[06:21] Priya: quick demo note: the apac latency run we'll run from your staging VPC using a lightweight harness — it's quick but requires a small token for API access.
[06:32] Mark: for the harness we need an IP whitelist and the peering details. i'll open a ticket post-call.
[06:40] Jordan: perfect. now, any concerns about data sovereignty? SummitCare has EU residency for PHI, right?
[06:49] Alice: EU data stays in eu-west-1, APAC will have non-PHI flows only, we can't send PHI to APAC. that's important.
[06:58] Priya: noted. we can enforce per-route policies and region pinning at the routing layer to ensure PHI stays in EU regions.
[07:08] Mark: about fallback — is there a predictable cutover window when apac fails and you route to us-west? we need <5s failover for interactive chat sessions.
[07:18] Priya: our routing policy supports fast failover with health checks — typically sub-2s detection and 3-5s warmup depending on cold start. we can pre-warm caches to get below 5s.
[07:31] Alice: good. re: contract terms, Sonal will want to see renewal pricing, termination clauses, and an SLA annex.
[07:38] Sonal: right, and our legal needs a clause about data deletion on termination.
[07:44] Jordan: we can add data deletion timeline in the amendment — default 90 days purge with expedited deletion option.
[07:51] Evan: adding the retention and deletion policy will be included in the draft amendment.
[07:57] Jordan: i'm going to share a rough cost sketch: 20% uplift + APAC geocluster as optional add-on adds roughly 18% to current committed spend, plus potential one-time provisioning fee for VPC peering.
[08:12] Sonal: 18% is within our exploratory budget; procurement will need line itemized quotes.
[08:20] Priya: i want to walk through the benchmark plan quickly: we'll run three scenarios — interactive chat (avg 40 tokens), reranking batch (avg 512 tokens), and embeddings (large batch). each run has 1,000 calls with synthetic replay of your traces.
[08:37] Alice: do we need to sanitize traces? we'll only share anonymized request ids and latencies.
[08:43] Priya: sanitzation is fine; we only need shape and size distribution.
[08:48] Mark: network egress — we will track egress to US for fallback; please include estimated egress cost in the bench sheet.
[08:56] Priya: will do.
[09:00] Jordan: any blockers on your side to proceed with the draft?
[09:05] Sonal: procurement wants the SOW by Friday and will push for a PO the week after if pricing is acceptable.
[09:12] Alice: engineering wants the APAC perf results before greenlight.
[09:16] Jordan: okay action items recap: Jordan send renewal amendment draft + pricing (due 2026-02-12); Priya run APAC benchmarks (due 2026-02-13); Mark share KMS and peering constraints (due 2026-02-17).
[09:29] Priya: small note on quality regressions — we'll attach eval sets. if you recall last Q we caught a generation drift after a model swap. we recommend pinning the model family in the contract until you have a stable baseline.
[09:44] Alice: yes we want to pin to a major version, with rollouts via canary and rollback hooks.
[09:50] Jordan: that's standard; we'll include rollout policies in the amendment.
[09:55] Evan: also adding monitoring retention — logs and traces for 90 days included, longer retention as add-on.
[10:03] Mark: what about dedicated throughput guarantees — can you commit to sustained throughput? there was a moment last month where we saw throttling.
[10:13] Priya: that was due to a configuration on the autoscalar; we put in a fix and recommend explicit reserved slots for critical routes. that will be in the SOW as reserved capacity lines.
[10:27] Jordan: ok, let's open it up for any random Qs.
[10:31] Alice: small ask — can you attach the last 3 months of token usage per route? helps us size uplift.
[10:38] Evan: i have that, will attach in the follow-up email.
[10:43] Sonal: timeline wise, if we sign amendment by 2/26, what's the earliest APAC activation?
[10:50] Jordan: with a standard provisioning lead time it's about 3 weeks for full VPC peered geocluster; hosted endpoints are faster: 3-5 days. we'll detail options in SOW.
[11:03] Priya: for testing we'll do hosted apac run first to validate perf, then stand up peered geocluster if you want private connectivity.
[11:14] Mark: ok that helps.
[11:17] Jordan: last thing — i'll include a comparison to BigCloud AI and Infralayer in the follow-up. any preference on format, table vs short bullets?
[11:26] Sonal: table please, with clear callouts on feature gaps like SOC2, KMS and KV cache.
[11:33] Jordan: copy that.
[11:36] Priya: i'll attach benchmark spreadsheet and a short runbook for APAC pre-warm steps.
[11:42] Alice: thanks. one more — can you confirm support coverage for weekends during the activation window? we had an incident last time.
[11:50] Evan: we'll add weekend oncall escalation for the provisioning week as part of the playbook.
[11:57] Sonal: great.
[12:00] Jordan: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the SOW and bench results.

(Transcript contains occasional ASR errors and mislabels; speaker turns approximate)
